200347690.title: Decoding super-enhancer regulatory grammar and pathogenic gain-of-function variants directly from DNA sequence
200347690.summary: Super-enhancers (SEs) drive cell-identity gene expression through clustered transcription factor (TF) assemblies. However, their identification relies heavily on empirical epigenomic profiling (e.g., H3K27ac ChIP-seq), obscuring the underlying sequence syntax and master TFs orchestrating these domains. Here, we present Cerberus, a deep learning framework built upon the genomic transformer Borzoi that formulates sequence-based SE discovery as hierarchical, cell-type-resolved genomic object detection across 90 human lineages. Base-resolution attribution enables Cerberus to de novo recover lineage-defining master TFs and reveal dynamic motif switching within regulatory domains shared across tissues. Using in silico ablation, Cerberus decoded the regulatory hierarchy of human globin locus control regions, prioritizing the dominant role of HS2 constituent—a dependency we experimentally corroborated via targeted CRISPR interference. Trained solely on wild-type genomes, Cerberus accurately predicted an oncogenic micro-insertion that nucleates a de novo super-enhancer upstream of TAL1 selectively in hematopoietic and T-ALL contexts. Furthermore, model-predicted variant impacts quantitatively calibrate empirical histone acetylation QTLs (haQTLs) across human tissues and uncover rare cardiac variants that nucleate super-enhancers via gain of NR3C1 motifs. Cerberus establishes a general framework for decoding super-enhancer regulatory grammar and prioritizing causal non-coding variants directly from sequence.
